name: Frac stack, standard configuration
function: The temporary stack of gate valves, cross, crown valve, flanged inlet block, and swab valve installed on the wellhead for the completion: it contains treating pressure, admits the spooled treating line, and gives wireline and coiled tubing access through the top.

tabs.overview:
Bottom to top in the standard configuration used on this site: tree adapter on the tubing head; lower master valve (manual, the last barrier, never cycled under flow); upper master valve (hydraulic, the working master); studded cross with a manual then a hydraulic wing valve on each side, wing A for pump-down and kill lines and wing B for flowback; crown valve (hydraulic) that isolates the well from everything above it; flanged inlet block where the spooled treating line from the zipper manifold enters; swab valve (hydraulic) that isolates the top; and a hands-free style top adapter for the wireline lubricator or the coiled tubing stack.

During fracturing the swab is closed, the crown, masters, and the zipper valve are open, and treating fluid enters at the inlet block and flows down. During wireline the zipper valve is closed, the swab is open, and the tool string passes down through the inlet block, crown, cross, and masters. The flanged inlet block replaces the goat head and its hammer-union iron; a single large-bore spool or monoline connects it to the zipper module.

Every valve is the same block-body gate valve family; the model can be shown in 4-1/16, 5-1/8, or 7-1/16 in. bore at 10K or 15K. Choose the size above the viewer.

For sliding sleeve completions the top adapter and lubricator are replaced by a ball launcher on the swab valve; the rest of the stack is unchanged (see WH-FRACTREE-BALLLAUNCHER).

tabs.engineering: All components are API 6A pressure-containing parts rated for the job working pressure. Bore is uniform through the stack so tools can pass. The lower master is the last barrier before the wellhead and is not cycled under pressure; the upper master is the working master and is actuated for emergency shut-in.
tabs.connections: Below: tubing head through the tree adapter. Side: wing A to the pump-down or kill line, wing B to the flowback line, both flanged. Inlet block: flanged hub to the treating spool from the zipper manifold. Top: hands-free adapter to the wireline pressure control stack or the coiled tubing injector stack.
tabs.safety: Operate valves in sequence: close the swab before pumping; open the wing to the frac line fully; never cycle the lower master under differential. Red zone around the tree during pumping. The stack is heavy; lifts use certified gear and no one stands under it.
tabs.specs: Working pressure 10K or 15K; bore 5-1/8 in. or 7-1/16 in.; height on the order of 12 to 20 ft depending on configuration (E4).
tabs.evidence: OEM configurations (S2, S3, S5, S11, S12); API 6A (S1); field practice (S9).
tabs.operations: Installed after the casing is landed and before the first wireline run; stays on the well through every stage, the drillout, and flowback; removed when the production tree is set. Pressure tested to the job pressure before the first run and after any connection is broken.
tabs.failure_modes: Erosion at the goat head inlets and the frac wing; valve seat wash; actuator failures; ring gasket leaks after repeated make-up.

hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
Restraints and whip checks on iron; exclusion zone around pressurized lines.
Tree saver in the wellhead; valves fully open or fully closed only; iron inspection.
Certified lifting gear; no personnel under suspended tree or lubricator sections.
